description: Cited thresholds the Weather Digital Twin buckets weather into (keys match ImpactKey in src/lib/musafir/twin.ts). Values are copied from the cited pages; unit conversions are shown with the factor used. The probabilities attached to each class are the twin's learned beliefs, not part of this dataset.

rainRate.note: AMS defines light / moderate / heavy. WMO states there is no agreed international definition of rainfall intensity and gives >50 mm/h as 'violent' for showers only, typical of tropical regions. There is no official lower bound for 'dry': AMS light rain starts at a trace, so any 'dry below X mm/h' cut-off is a product choice, not a cited value.

sources.quote: 1) “light,” the rate of fall varying between a trace and 0.25 cm (0.10 in.) per hour … 2) “moderate,” from 0.26 to 0.76 cm (0.11 to 0.30 in.) per hour … 3) “heavy,” over 0.76 cm (0.30 in.) per hour

While there is no agreed international definition regarding rainfall intensity … Showers are further classified as being violent if the rate exceeds 50 mm per hour, although these are normally considered to be rates typical for tropical regions.

heatIndex.note: NWS bands are for the heat index. Musafir applies them to Open-Meteo's apparent temperature, which is a related but different measure; label it 'feels like', not 'heat index'.

classes.label: Caution
classes.effect: Fatigue possible with prolonged exposure and/or physical activity

classes.label: Extreme Caution
classes.effect: Heat stroke, heat cramps, or heat exhaustion possible with prolonged exposure and/or physical activity

classes.label: Danger
classes.effect: Heat cramps or heat exhaustion likely, and heat stroke possible with prolonged exposure and/or physical activity

sources.quote: Caution 80°F - 90°F … Extreme Caution 90°F - 103°F … Danger 103°F - 124°F … Extreme Danger 125°F or higher: Heat stroke highly likely

wind.note: The Beaufort scale classifies MEAN wind speed. Musafir compares gusts against the force 7 / 9 lower bounds; gusts run higher than the mean, so that is a conservative approximation, not the scale's own definition.

sources.quote: Beaufort wind scale — Mean Wind Speed — Limits of wind speed (Knots): 6 22-27 Strong breeze; 7 28-33 Near gale; 8 34-40 Gale; 9 41-47 Strong gale; 10 48-55 Storm; 11 56-63 Violent storm; 12 64+ Hurricane
7 28-33 Near Gale … 8 34-40 Gale … 9 41-47 Strong Gale … 10 48-55 Storm
